check: Choose Files in the sandboxed Mac app's Share Inbox, driven through the Accessibility API by process ID: the open panel appears, and the chosen files wait for review in order with their origins
limitations: An agent drove the run through the Accessibility API and posted key events; no person used a pointer, and VoiceOver was not running.

It proves the Mac host's file-picker fallback on this Mac only. LAB-007's declared surfaces are iPhone and iPad with a share extension, which this run does not touch, so the experiment stays implemented.
Only files were chosen, and this build cannot add files to a collection, so no receipt was made. Adding pasted text and links is proven by the hosted tests.
The files came from a local folder; no iCloud Drive or other file provider was used, so no download was waited on or cancelled.
The pasteboard was not used, and drag and drop onto the inbox was not run.
The container's inbox already held two file imports from an earlier session's run under the same bundle prefix; they were left as they were and are not part of this record.

outcome.detail: The open panel appeared each time Choose Files… was pressed, and Open imported the selection. The first Open staged gull-count.txt: the inbox read “1 item is waiting for review.” and listed “gull-count.txt, File, File picker, …, Can't be added in this version”. The second Open, of the three fixture files, read “2 items are waiting for review, 1 was already waiting.”: gull-count.txt was a duplicate and kept its first origin, and harbor-sketch.png and tide-clip.mov were listed as File picker, 2 of 3 and 3 of 3. The movie's review screen read Came through: File picker; Position: 3 of 3 shared together; Declared type: com.apple.quicktime-movie; Adds as: App UI; and “Files are checked and kept for review, but this version can’t add files to a collection yet.” An earlier Open in the same run, of a mistaken selection of 19 entries in a scratch folder, refused the 8 folders by position as not ordinary files and staged the 11 files at their positions; those imports were removed at once, and no name or content from them is recorded.

steps: xcodebuild -scheme LabMac-Core -configuration Debug build at 074eaaa, under a separate bundle prefix set in an ignored Config/Local.xcconfig, so the app used its own container; codesign showed com.apple.security.app-sandbox and com.apple.security.files.user-selected.read-write
open -n on the built app; its process ID taken from its exact executable path; every later action addressed that process ID
View › Share Inbox, pressed as a menu item through the Accessibility API
Choose Files… pressed through the Accessibility API; the open panel appeared as a sheet on the window

In the panel: Go to Folder (⌘⇧G, posted only while that process was frontmost), its path field set through the Accessibility API to a copy of intake/gull-count.txt in a scratch folder outside the repository, Return, then Open pressed

Choose Files… again: Go to Folder to the copy of intake/harbor-sketch.png in the same folder, ⌘A to select that folder's three files (intake/gull-count.txt, intake/harbor-sketch.png, intake/tide-clip.mov), then Open
The movie's row selected through the Accessibility API and its review screen read
Each test import removed with Remove from Inbox and its confirmation; only the launched process was stopped
subject: LAB-007
